reference.title: Dumbbell Standing Hands Torsion (male)
reference.listing: Video; the page could not be read here (blocked). The movement follows the name and a written description of the same catalog exercise: one dumbbell upright in both hands in front of the body, rotated through the forearms and wrists with the elbows by the ribs.

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily; out as the dumbbell tips to each side, in as it comes back through upright.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s to each side, 2 s across

prescription.tempo: Slow and controlled; brief pause at each end
prescription.load: User-chosen light dumbbell; the lever arm grows as it tips
prescription.progression: Longer pauses at each end, then a heavier dumbbell or holding nearer one end

cues.text: Stand tall. Hold one dumbbell upright in front of the belly, one fist above the other; elbows bent and by the ribs, wrists straight.
Turn the forearms so the top of the dumbbell tips out to the right; upper arms stay still.
Pause at the end of the range you can control.
Turn back through upright and tip it out to the left.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the arms or twisting the trunk to move the dumbbell
mistakes.fix: Pin the elbows to the ribs; only the forearms turn.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the dumbbell drop at the end of the range
mistakes.fix: Go only as far as you can stop it; use a lighter dumbbell.
Keep the wrists in line with the forearms; the turn comes from the forearm.

kinematics.norm: About 40-45 degrees each way from upright (clinical opinion)
Functional forearm rotation needs about 50 degrees each of pronation and supination (Ryu 1991 studied the wrist; forearm values are clinical opinion)
Bent and by the ribs, still (clinical opinion)
Slow, controlled, pause at each end (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #17299, Dumbbell Standing Hands Torsion (male), video (movement reference)
Ryu, Cooney, Askew, An and Chao 1991, functional ranges of motion of the wrist joint (J Hand Surg Am 16(3):409-419; 40 adults, biaxial wrist electrogoniometer)
Effectiveness of different methods of resistance exercises in lateral epicondylosis, a systematic review (J Hand Ther 2012;25(1):5-25; PubMed 22075055; 12 studies)
Szymanski, Szymanski, Molloy and Pascoe 2004, effect of 12 weeks of wrist and forearm training on high school baseball players (J Strength Cond Res 18(3):432-440; PubMed 15320673; 43 players)

cautions: Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Elbow or wrist pain (for example tennis or golfer's elbow): use a very light dumbbell or none, and a small range.
Hold the dumbbell firmly and keep it away from the body; a long dumbbell tips quickly.
Stand clear of anything you could hit if the dumbbell slips.
modify: Hold the dumbbell near one end for less lever, or use a hammer or a light bar.
Seated, forearms resting on the thighs.
regressions: No weight: turn the fists through the same range.

muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Pronator teres and the wrist flexors turn the forearm palm-down and grip the handle (clinical opinion). Forearm strengthening is a mainstay for lateral elbow pain (J Hand Ther 2012 review).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Pronator teres and the wrist flexors turn the forearm palm-down and grip the handle (clinical opinion). Forearm strengthening is a mainstay for lateral elbow pain (J Hand Ther 2012 review).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Supinator and brachioradialis (drawn with the extensors) turn the forearm palm-up and hold the wrists straight (clinical opinion). Wrist and forearm training improved forearm strength in Szymanski 2004.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Supinator and brachioradialis (drawn with the extensors) turn the forearm palm-up and hold the wrists straight (clinical opinion). Wrist and forearm training improved forearm strength in Szymanski 2004.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Assists supination and holds the elbows bent (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Assists supination and holds the elbows bent (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arms still (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arms still (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Upper fist tips right, then left
